candidate_statement: AWWA's reported predecessor may have begun as a cross-community welfare body rather than a purely military-spouse organization.
supporting_observation: A contributed history says the Ryukyu American Welfare Council brought Okinawan and American women together to provide grants to Japanese nonprofits.
competing_explanation_or_test: Check USCAR, Okinawa Prefectural Archives, contemporary directories and predecessor bylaws for composition, legal continuity and exact name.
claim_limit: Do not state that current AWWA is legally identical to the 1952 body or that all participants were equally represented.

candidate_statement: Reversion may have reorganized the welfare intermediary from a mixed predecessor into a federation centered on U.S. military spouse clubs.
supporting_observation: Community history says service spouses formed AWWA after reversion; a local newspaper independently dates AWWA's establishment to 1972 by U.S. military personnel and wives.
competing_explanation_or_test: Test whether the apparent boundary change followed sovereignty/legal rules, base private-organization regulation, personnel turnover, or only a change in naming/documentation.
claim_limit: This is a reorganization hypothesis, not proof that reversion caused social separation.

candidate_statement: AWWA pools revenue generated by spouse-club gift and thrift shops and redistributes it to American and Okinawan welfare recipients.
supporting_observation: Current and historical descriptions identify five member spouse organizations and shop-derived charitable funds.
competing_explanation_or_test: Compare annual recipient composition and allocation rules against public base-policy controversy cycles.
claim_limit: The complete recipient table and annual amounts are not available; do not extrapolate from named examples.

candidate_statement: AWWA publicly frames welfare giving as community impact, Japan-U.S. exchange and goodwill.
supporting_observation: AWWA-associated and newspaper narratives explicitly describe local-community contribution, exchange and goodwill.
competing_explanation_or_test: Compare this goodwill frame with recipient-authored accounts and with periods of heightened base controversy.
claim_limit: Goodwill language is not evidence of support for base policy and does not establish recipient attitudes.

candidate_statement: OESC's island-wide form arose from an unmet cross-service enlisted-spouse support need rather than from a base-policy campaign.
supporting_observation: Air Force public affairs reports that Kadena Enlisted Spouses Club became Okinawa Enlisted Spouses Club and opened to enlisted spouses across all branches after a Marine spouse found no suitable enlisted-spouse club.
competing_explanation_or_test: Check archived bylaws, prior club pages and IRS filings for the formal transition and predecessor continuity.
claim_limit: The account is a public-affairs narrative and does not alone prove why every participant joined or that no prior informal network existed.

candidate_statement: Long-term garrison presence generates recurring needs for belonging, emergency communication, financial relief, transitions and disaster support.
supporting_observation: USO reports six centers serving about 47,000 service members and families; OESC, Red Cross and NMCRS describe complementary care functions.
competing_explanation_or_test: Compare Okinawa with installations of different scale and duration; test whether these forms are Okinawa-specific or standard overseas-garrison infrastructure.
claim_limit: Observed functions do not establish a simple causal claim that the base alone produced each organization.

candidate_statement: The official private-organization universe contains many professional, recreational, school, fraternal and service groups, so the nine service-core actors are a selected functional subset rather than the whole base-associated civic ecology.
supporting_observation: MCCS lists numerous authorized non-federal private organizations and marks MOSCO active among a much broader universe.
competing_explanation_or_test: Use the complete directory as a denominator and compare which organizational forms enter the registry, receive public coverage or create local recipient ties.
claim_limit: Do not call all directory entries NGOs or infer their legal, political or charitable status from directory presence.

candidate_statement: The apparent divide may be between base-accountability advocacy and welfare/administrative service fields, not between U.S.-connected organizations and Okinawan civil society as wholes.
supporting_observation: AWWA has documented support relationships with Ambitious and municipal welfare councils, while the bounded exact-name search found no direct interface with the 18 accountability anchors.
competing_explanation_or_test: Crosswalk full recipients against general-welfare, administrative and accountability actor universes using identical inclusion rules.
claim_limit: Current recipient coverage is incomplete and the accountability-side search tests indexed public co-mentions, not all social contact.

candidate_statement: Separated English military-service channels and Japanese advocacy channels may manufacture an apparent network gap in web-derived data.
supporting_observation: Service actors are documented mainly by English organization, military public-affairs and tax pages; accountability anchors are documented mainly by Japanese movement, legal and local-news sources.
competing_explanation_or_test: Run bilingual name/entity resolution on common event, recipient, officer and venue records; compare channel-matched samples.
claim_limit: This is a measurement explanation, not an observed social relationship.

candidate_statement: Military-family rotation may place cross-organization bridges in short-lived personal biographies rather than durable organization pages.
supporting_observation: A public professional-profile search produced a lead for one individual listing roles across several spouse/service organizations, but no independent second source was obtained.
competing_explanation_or_test: Build dated officer/volunteer rosters from Form 990, archived organization pages and official stories; require two sources before person-overlap coding.
claim_limit: Do not identify the lead as a verified shared-person edge and do not infer a cross-accountability bridge.

candidate_statement: Registry scope may hide service-to-local interfaces because many welfare recipients are outside the base-accountability actor registry while remaining visible in administrative records.
supporting_observation: Ambitious and municipal welfare institutions appear as AWWA recipients, but they are not members of the 18-actor accountability anchor set.
competing_explanation_or_test: Repeat interface measurement using a three-layer universe: accountability advocacy, base-associated service/charity, and general welfare/administrative organizations.
claim_limit: Do not treat source labels in the 616-row S002 universe as verified actor identities or approved relations.
